+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '80'
+title: 'SelectionConfig: the default preamble makes a 4B model answer an empty list for a function catalog'
+---
+## What
+
+Measured in FoundationModelsMultitool (card ^zqz1zan, 2026-09-09) on `mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-4bit`: the under-budget path, one grammar-constrained call per query, a 9-entry tool catalog (files read/write/edit/patch/glob/grep, shell execute/getLines/grepHistory), the intent under `# Task`.
+
+| preamble | queries answered, of 10 | note |
+|---|---|---|
+| `.selectionDefault` | 2 | eight `{"ids":[]}`; every query for a way to write, edit or run a command came back empty |
+| `.librarianDefault` (registry) | 10 | over-selects: 9 of 9 ids for "run pytest tests, execute" and for "file operations: create, write, append, delete, move" |
+| consumer preamble (below) | 10 | `shell.execute` alone for "run pytest tests, execute"; `files.write`, `files.edit`, `files.read` for "write file, edit file, create file" |
+
+The consumer preamble: "The candidates below are the functions a program can call, each under its id. Given a task, answer with the ids of the candidates the program calls to do that task — the fewest that suffice, in call order when order matters. Prefer the closest candidates over an empty answer; answer with an empty list only when no candidate is related to the task at all."
+
+The grammar, the prompt and the blocks were the same in all runs. The consumer now passes this text as `SelectionConfig(model:preamble:)`. That is the seam the config offers, but the default is what every other consumer gets, and on a small model the default answers nothing.
+
+Note: the Ranker card "One demo query returns no match on a cold selection session" measured a V2 wording ("return an empty list only when no candidate is related to the task") on the system model and found that it did not fix that cold-session defect. This card is a different measurement: a 4B MLX model, a warm cached root, and a wording that also says what the candidates are and what an answer is.
+
+## Where to look
+
+- `Selection/SelectionConfig.swift`: `.selectionDefault` (lines 163-166 in the checkout of 2026-09-09).
+- `IntegrationTests/Tests/FoundationModelsRankerIntegrationTests/ZeroConfigSearcherRealModelTests.swift`: the demo queries that must keep their answers.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] Measure the default and the consumer wording on the ranker's own live suite (system model) and, if one is reachable, on a 4B MLX model, over the demo queries and the ten queries of the consumer card.
+- [ ] Change `.selectionDefault`, or add a named preamble for function catalogs, so a 4B model answers a query that a candidate serves. Record the counts on this card.
+- [ ] Tell the consumer: FoundationModelsMultitool can then drop its own constant `SearchToolsTool.selectionPreamble`.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] The live suite keeps its cold-session answers.
+- [ ] A live test on the ten consumer queries, or a subset, answers at least the queries that name a candidate.

+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m250srkh454atf379ke4smv5
+  text: |-
+    ### Measurement (2026-09-10)
+
+    Three wordings, three rounds each. The demo set is the four `FullMonty` queries over the 50-item demo catalog. The consumer set is the ten queries of card ^zqz1zan over the nine-function catalog (files read, write, edit, patch, glob, grep; shell execute, getLines, grepHistory).
+
+    The wordings:
+
+    - `current`: the default that shipped before this card. "Given a task, return ONLY the items needed — fewest that suffice, in call order when order matters. Do not invent ids; return an empty list if nothing fits."
+    - `consumer`: `SearchToolsTool.selectionPreamble` from FoundationModelsMultitool.
+    - `neutral`: the new default. "The candidates below are the items available to do a task, each under its id. Given a task, answer with the ids of the candidates that do it — the fewest that suffice, in call order when order matters. Use only the ids shown. Prefer the closest candidates over an empty answer; answer with an empty list only when no candidate is related to the task at all."
+
+    **System model** (on-device `SystemLanguageModel.default`, a bare `LanguageModelSession`, no grammar, one-line summaries from `LiveToolCatalog`):
+
+    | wording | demo, cold `Searcher` for each query | consumer, cold tier for each query | consumer, one cached root for all ten | ids not in the catalog |
+    |---|---|---|---|---|
+    | current | 12 of 12 | 27 of 30 | 30 of 30 | 0 |
+    | consumer | 12 of 12 | 30 of 30 | 30 of 30 | 2 |
+    | neutral | 12 of 12 | 30 of 30 | 30 of 30 | 1 |
+
+    The three empty answers of `current` are all q9, "file operations: create, write, append, delete, move", cold, 0 of 3. The same query on a cached root answered 3 of 3.
+
+    **`mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-4bit`** (FoundationModelsRouter, the consumer's own `MetadataIndex` catalog and `idEnumGrammar`, one cached root for each set, run through a temporary test in `FoundationModelsMultitool/IntegrationTests`, then deleted):
+
+    | wording | demo | consumer |
+    |---|---|---|
+    | current | 12 of 12 | 0 of 30 |
+    | consumer | 12 of 12 | 30 of 30 |
+    | neutral | 12 of 12 | 30 of 30 |
+
+    With `current`, the 4B model answered `{"ids":[]}` for all ten consumer queries in all three rounds. That is worse than the 2 of 10 the consumer card recorded, and the direction is the same. With `neutral` and with `consumer`, the answers were the same picks: `shell.execute` alone for "run pytest tests, execute", `files.write`, `files.edit`, `files.read` for "write file, edit file, create file", and six ids for "file operations: create, write, append, delete, move".
+
+    Note on the 4B run: the ranker checkout in the Multitool build is `5ab7b1a`, which is two commits behind the local ranker HEAD. The prefix and the prompt are the same in both revisions. The older tier drops a pick the retrieval ranking does not hold, so the temporary test gave it a placeholder ranking over every id.
+
+    **Decision**: change `.selectionDefault` to the `neutral` wording. It answers as well as the consumer wording on both models, and it keeps the words `items` and `ids` and no `function`. No named function-catalog preamble is needed.
+
+    **RED and GREEN**: the new live test `FunctionCatalogRealModelTests` failed on q9 with the old default (`matches → []`) and passed 10 of 10 with the new default. Then `swift build --build-tests` (no warnings), `swift test` (282 tests, 22 suites, passed), and `swift test --package-path IntegrationTests` (5 tests, 5 suites, passed).
